findings.title: Deployment orders-cdc/cdc-orders: chronic OOMKills (50 restarts)
findings.summary: Pods keep restarting (up to 50 times) and restarted again within the last hour. Each OOMKill drops in-flight work (for log shippers: buffered logs). The memory limit is too low for the steady-state load, or there is a leak.
evidence: cdc-orders-7f4c9d2a1b-q8wzn [OOMKilled, node ip-10-0-1-11.ec2.internal]: container app restarted 7m ago (OOMKilled), restarts=50; Ready again now
last restart 7m ago

steps.description: Read the crash output from the previous container instance
Check exit code, reason and limits

verify: kubectl get pods -n orders-cdc | grep cdc-orders

findings.title: StatefulSet confluent/ksqldb-cluster-1: uses 14.6Gi memory with no memory request
findings.summary: The scheduler places pods by their requests, so it sees this workload as needing no memory at all while it uses 14.6Gi. The nodes it lands on get packed past their capacity, which is what node memory alerts report. Pods using more memory than they request are evicted before pods that stay within their request.
evidence: requests per pod: memory none, cpu none; memory limit none; QoS Burstable
the app containers set no requests; QoS is Burstable only because an init container sets some
ksqldb-cluster-1-1 [node ip-10-0-1-11.ec2.internal, 24% of its memory]: memory 14.6Gi (requested none), cpu 321m (requested none)
ksqldb-cluster-1-0 [node ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal, 24% of its memory]: memory 14.2Gi (requested none), cpu 337m (requested none)
pod template owned by KsqlDB ksqldb-cluster-1 (platform.confluent.io/v1beta1): edits to the statefulset are reverted by the operator
usage is one metrics-server sample (memory = working set, includes active page cache)

steps.description: Confirm the numbers against p95/peak usage over 7-14 days (Sysdig) before applying; this scan saw a single sample. Proposed starting point: requests: {memory: 17920Mi}, limits: {memory: 17920Mi}

Set the resources in the Confluent for Kubernetes KsqlDB CR "ksqldb-cluster-1" under spec.podTemplate.resources (CFK owns the statefulset and reverts direct edits); for Kafka/Connect/ksqlDB also align the JVM heap (-Xmx) with the new limit

verify: kubectl get pods -n confluent -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,QOS:.status.qosClass | grep ksqldb-cluster-1
